_note: Each traffic-pattern and landing-runway rule's boundaries, written down from AC 90-66C, 14 CFR 91.126 and the AIM, never from the code. Shape and checks as engine/facade/tests/common/cases.rs says; asked by engine/facade/tests/rule_cases.rs.

cases.name: Left traffic on 27, coming from the south: the pattern's side, on the 45 abeam midfield
cases.source: AC 90-66C (2023) 11.3, Traffic Pattern Entry: "Entry to the downwind leg should be at a 45-degree angle abeam the midpoint of the runway to be used for landing." Left traffic landing west puts the downwind south of the runway (91.126(b)(1)).

cases.name: Left traffic on 27, coming from the north: the other side
cases.source: AC 90-66C Appendix A-5: from the upwind (other) side, the preferred and the alternate midfield entries (FAA-H-8083-3C ch. 7).

cases.name: Leaving right traffic: straight out or a 45 to the right
cases.source: AC 90-66C 11.8 and Appendix A's key, item 6: "If departing the traffic pattern, continue straight out, or exit with a 45-degree turn (to the left when in a left-hand traffic pattern; to the right when in a right-hand traffic pattern) beyond the departure end of the runway, after reaching pattern altitude."

cases.name: Leaving left traffic: a 45 to the left
cases.source: AC 90-66C 11.8 and Appendix A's key, item 6: "If departing the traffic pattern, continue straight out, or exit with a 45-degree turn (to the left when in a left-hand traffic pattern; to the right when in a right-hand traffic pattern) beyond the departure end of the runway, after reaching pattern altitude."

cases.name: Landing 09 in left traffic: five legs, the downwind north, the final to the threshold
cases.source: AC 90-66C Appendix A, the traffic pattern's legs: upwind, crosswind, downwind, base and final, the final "along the extended runway centerline from the base leg to the runway"; 14 CFR 91.126(b)(1): left unless marked right.

cases.name: Landing 27 in right traffic: the downwind north too
cases.source: AC 90-66C Appendix A, the traffic pattern's legs: upwind, crosswind, downwind, base and final, the final "along the extended runway centerline from the base leg to the runway"; 14 CFR 91.126(b)(1): left unless marked right. Right traffic landing west turns right, to the north.

cases.name: The 45 joins the downwind abeam midfield
cases.source: AC 90-66C (2023) 11.3, Traffic Pattern Entry: "Entry to the downwind leg should be at a 45-degree angle abeam the midpoint of the runway to be used for landing." Midfield of a runway from 0 to 1/60 degree of longitude is 1/120.

cases.name: No threshold surveyed: no pattern drawn
cases.source: NASR APT_RWY_END's threshold position: a pattern drawn without it would be drawn somewhere it is not.

cases.name: Departing 09 toward the east: straight out
cases.source: AC 90-66C 11.8 and Appendix A's key, item 6: "If departing the traffic pattern, continue straight out, or exit with a 45-degree turn (to the left when in a left-hand traffic pattern; to the right when in a right-hand traffic pattern) beyond the departure end of the runway, after reaching pattern altitude."

cases.name: Departing 09 toward the north in left traffic: the 45 to the left
cases.source: AC 90-66C 11.8 and Appendix A's key, item 6: "If departing the traffic pattern, continue straight out, or exit with a 45-degree turn (to the left when in a left-hand traffic pattern; to the right when in a right-hand traffic pattern) beyond the departure end of the runway, after reaching pattern altitude."

cases.name: UGN 5's arrival lands on its threshold
cases.source: AC 90-66C Appendix A, the traffic pattern's legs: upwind, crosswind, downwind, base and final, the final "along the extended runway centerline from the base leg to the runway"; 14 CFR 91.126(b)(1): left unless marked right. NASR's "05" is runway 5 (AIM 2-3-3).

cases.name: UGN 5's departure toward a point ahead leaves straight out
cases.source: AC 90-66C 11.8 and Appendix A's key, item 6: "If departing the traffic pattern, continue straight out, or exit with a 45-degree turn (to the left when in a left-hand traffic pattern; to the right when in a right-hand traffic pattern) beyond the departure end of the runway, after reaching pattern altitude."
cases.method: The runway's own bearing, threshold to threshold, worked on a sphere; the point ahead 30 nm along it.

cases.name: UGN 5's departure toward a point 60 degrees left: the 45 to the left
cases.source: AC 90-66C 11.8 and Appendix A's key, item 6: "If departing the traffic pattern, continue straight out, or exit with a 45-degree turn (to the left when in a left-hand traffic pattern; to the right when in a right-hand traffic pattern) beyond the departure end of the runway, after reaching pattern altitude."

cases.name: A straight-in approach to 9 lands on 9, a pick of 27 set aside
cases.source: AIM 5-4-20, Approach and Landing Minimums: a straight-in approach lands on the runway it is aligned with; circling minimums let the airplane circle to another; 14 CFR 91.175, the runway of intended landing.

cases.name: With circling minimums the pilot's 27 stands
cases.source: AIM 5-4-20, Approach and Landing Minimums: a straight-in approach lands on the runway it is aligned with; circling minimums let the airplane circle to another; 14 CFR 91.175, the runway of intended landing.

cases.name: A pick into the wind, not the pilot's, gives way to the approach's own
cases.source: AIM 5-4-20, Approach and Landing Minimums: a straight-in approach lands on the runway it is aligned with; circling minimums let the airplane circle to another; 14 CFR 91.175, the runway of intended landing.

cases.name: The plate still coming is taken as no circling
cases.source: AIM 5-4-20, Approach and Landing Minimums: a straight-in approach lands on the runway it is aligned with; circling minimums let the airplane circle to another; 14 CFR 91.175, the runway of intended landing.

cases.name: No approach: the pick stands
cases.source: AIM 5-4-20, Approach and Landing Minimums: a straight-in approach lands on the runway it is aligned with; circling minimums let the airplane circle to another; 14 CFR 91.175, the runway of intended landing.
